# Gestational Carrier — Authorization Guide

_CPT Codes · ICD-10 · Payer Requirements_

(backHref: /gestational-carrier)

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | Party |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 58970 | Follicle puncture for oocyte retrieval (intended mother) | Intended Mother |
| 58974 | Embryo transfer, intrauterine (gestational carrier) | Carrier |
| 58976 | Gamete, zygote, or embryo intrafallopian transfer | Carrier |
| 89250 | Culture of oocyte(s)/embryo(s), less than 4 days | Lab |
| 89253 | Assisted embryo hatching, microtechnique | Lab |
| 89280 | Assisted oocyte fertilization (ICSI), microtechnique; ≤10 oocytes | Lab |
| 89337 | Cryopreservation, mature oocyte(s) | Lab |
| 89352 | Thawing of cryopreserved; oocyte(s) | Lab |
| 89353 | Thawing of cryopreserved; embryo(s) | Lab |
| 76830 | Ultrasound, transvaginal (carrier monitoring) | Carrier |

**Billing Note**

Services for the intended mother (egg retrieval, stimulation) are billed under her insurance. Services for the gestational carrier (embryo transfer, monitoring) are billed under the carrier's insurance or self-pay. Confirm coverage for each party separately.

## ICD-10 Diagnoses

| ICD-10 | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Q51.0 | Agenesis and aplasia of uterus (MRKH syndrome) |
| Q51.810 | Arcuate uterus |
| N85.6 | Intrauterine synechiae (Asherman syndrome) |
| Z90.710 | Acquired absence of uterus with remaining cervical stump |
| Z90.711 | Acquired absence of uterus with remaining cervical stump |
| Z90.712 | Acquired absence of both uterus and cervix |
| N97.2 | Female infertility of uterine origin |
| Z31.83 | Encounter for assisted reproductive fertility procedure cycle |

## Coverage Landscape

**Coverage Reality**

- Gestational carrier procedures are almost universally excluded from commercial insurance
- Most plans explicitly exclude "surrogacy" in benefit language
- Even in states with fertility mandates, gestational carrier is often excluded
- Self-pay is the norm; average cost $50,000–$150,000 total

**When Appeals May Succeed**

- Absolute uterine factor (MRKH, surgical absence): strongest medical necessity argument
- Medical contraindication to pregnancy (e.g., pulmonary hypertension, cardiac disease)
- Some self-insured employer plans (ERISA) may cover gestational carrier
- Intended mother's IVF services (egg retrieval, stimulation) may be covered separately

## Prior Authorization Requirements

### Required Documentation

- Documentation of uterine factor (surgical report, imaging, pathology)
- For MRKH: karyotype, pelvic MRI or ultrasound confirming uterine absence
- For medical contraindication: specialist documentation (cardiology, pulmonology)
- ASRM-compliant gestational carrier screening documentation
- Legal agreement between intended parents and carrier
- Letter of medical necessity from REI specialist
- Separate authorization for intended mother's IVF services
